channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: EUA trocam chefe de escritório que supervisiona América Latina
item.description: The U.S. government announced a leadership change in the bureau overseeing U.S. relations with Brazil and Latin America, with Juan Pablo Segura assuming the role of Assistant Secretary of State for Western Hemisphere Affairs, succeeding Michael Kozak. The shift comes amid deteriorating U.S.-Brazil relations, following the U.S. cancellation of the visa for Brazilian Ambassador Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti, in response to Brazil’s delay in approving Daniel Perez as U.S. ambassador to Brazil.

item.title: Por que projeto de exploração de petróleo na Foz do Amazonas é controverso?
item.description: Petrobras announced the discovery of oil in the Foz do Rio Amazonas basin, in ultra-deep waters off the coast of Amapá, confirming its optimism about Brazil’s equatorial margin. Although the find does not yet indicate immediate economic viability, the company states that any future exploration would use advanced technology to ensure operational safety and environmental care. The project is controversial due to the region’s ecological sensitivity, facing opposition from environmental groups and internal government debate over energy transition and continued reliance on fossil fuels.

item.title: Usina de Pivetta recebeu de empresas citadas pela PF no acordo da Oi
item.description: Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos), the governor of Mato Grosso running for re-election, owns Brasbio Brasil Bioenergia S/A, a plant that received R$37 million from partners linked to the Federal Police’s Operation Heritage, which investigates the misdirection of state funds in a deal with telecom company Oi. The agreement, signed in April 2024 under former governor Mauro Mendes (União) — now a Senate candidate — paid Oi R$308 million without following the legal creditor queue, allegedly using 15 funds to conceal the money. Pivetta denies any wrongdoing, while Mendes claims the deal was lawful.

item.title: Lula lança jingle após chamar apoiadores para programarem despertadores
item.description: President Lula launched a new jingle on social media after asking supporters to set their alarms for 5:13 a.m., symbolizing the start of a new dawn for Brazil. The video, depicting workers waking early, emphasizes courage and hard work, with the chorus 'It’s Lula again for us to shine!'. The 2026 electoral campaign has begun, and the TSE has set rules for online political advertising, including bans on paid influencer promotions and requirements for transparency in AI use.

item.title: 1 a cada 5 candidatos de 2026 é milionário; percentual é recorde
item.description: 18.6% of the 20,530 candidates registered by August 17, 2026 declared assets of R$1 million or more, a historical high, with the Liberal Party leading in absolute numbers (30.4% of its candidates are millionaires) and Tocantins showing the highest state proportion (30.3%). Despite a 29.8% drop in total candidates compared to 2022, the share of wealthy candidates remains elevated, though asset declarations are noted as unreliable due to lack of audit.

item.title: Foi um bom começo?
item.description: The first day of the 2026 Brazilian presidential campaign received overwhelmingly positive feedback for Lula, with 86.4% of readers rating his start as good, compared to only 9.8% for Flávio Bolsonaro. A small minority (3.8%) viewed both candidates’ openings as merely average, reflecting a clear early advantage for Lula in public perception.

item.title: Justiça em Londres ignora decisão do Supremo e segue com Lava Jato
item.description: London’s Crown Court ruled that the UK’s Serious Fraud Office (SFO) may continue using evidence obtained in Brazil during Operation Lava Jato to justify the civil forfeiture of £7.3 million from Mario Ildeu de Miranda, a former Petrobras engineer, despite Brazilian Minister Dias Toffoli annulling in March 2026 the legal basis for sharing such evidence. Judge Mark Weekes described the situation as 'highly unusual,' noting that a Brazilian judicial authority had formally revoked the legal foundation for mutual legal assistance after the evidence had already been shared. Miranda’s appeal against the asset freeze, filed in September 2025, resumed in May 2026 following additional inquiries with Brazilian authorities.

item.title: Na campanha de Lula, revelações sobre Lulinha são vistas como 'fatos gravíssimos'
item.description: The relationship between Fabio Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger is becoming a growing concern for the federal government. Revelations about this connection are being described as 'very serious facts' within President Lula's re-election campaign, potentially affecting public perception of transparency and ethics. The subscriber-only article suggests these ties could have significant political and legal implications.

item.title: Candidatos da família Bolsonaro declaram de R$ 158 mil a R$ 8 milhões
item.description: Eight members of the Bolsonaro family are set to run for office in the 2026 elections, having declared assets ranging from R$ 158,000 to R$ 8 million to the TSE. This wide wealth range reflects varying levels of financial accumulation among the former president’s relatives. The declarations were submitted as part of their official candidate registration.

item.title: Flávio imita Lula e deve descartar debates para evitar virar alvo
item.description: The teams of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) are considering skipping debates and interviews in the early phase of the 2026 campaign to avoid becoming primary targets of attacks and to prevent opponents from creating viral social media content. The first debate, hosted by Rede Bandeirantes, is scheduled for Sunday, March 23.

item.title: Os números de Lula e Flávio nas redes no primeiro dia de campanha
item.description: On the first day of the 2026 presidential campaign, Lula outperformed Flávio Bolsonaro in social media engagement, recording 3.6 million interactions and 22 million views compared to 2.4 million and 15.9 million, respectively. Lula also received a higher share of positive mentions (70% vs 57%) and drew a significantly larger crowd at his campaign launch (40,000 according to the PT vs 8,900 estimated by USP for Flávio).

item.title: Com Lula, Alcolumbre embarca no discurso de soberania nacional
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP) aligned with President Lula’s national sovereignty rhetoric by celebrating Petrobras’ oil discovery in the Equatorial Margin during an event in Amapá. He credited Lula for advancing exploration in Amapá’s coast and for supporting key government agendas in the Senate, marking their first public meeting since renewing dialogue. Lula framed the discovery as a 'passport to the future' and reinforced the government’s narrative of asserting Brazilian control over strategic resources amid tensions with foreign powers, particularly the U.S.

item.title: Meta AI, Grok, Gemini e ChatGPT espalham desinformação e imprecisões sobre eleições, mostra estudo
item.description: A study by Ekō found that popular AI chatbots — Meta AI, Grok, Gemini, and ChatGPT — spread misinformation and gave inaccurate responses about Brazil’s 2026 elections, with Meta AI showing the highest error rate at 24%, including false claims about Bolsonaro’s convictions and non-existent TSE contacts. Tests using three voter profiles (bolsonarist, petist, and neutral) asking 25 questions each revealed that the models produced partially or entirely incorrect answers, including vote recommendations and conspiracy theories.

item.title: MP pede que Justiça barre candidatura de deputado por ligação com jogo do bicho
item.description: The Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office requested that the Justice block the candidacy of state deputy Jamilson Name (PP-MS) for re-election due to his links to the illegal gambling game 'jogo do bicho' and his conviction for organized crime and money laundering. The MP stated that Name led the illegal operation in Mato Grosso do Sul and declared R$ 36 million in assets, which, according to the TSE, is sufficient to bar his candidacy even without a final criminal conviction.

item.title: 'Geração Lava Jato' prefere Flávio, e idosos podem ser 'novo Nordeste' de Lula, diz diretora do Datafolha
item.description: Datafolha director Luciana Chong highlighted that voters aged 60+ are now the largest electoral bloc in history and show strong support for Lula, with 55% favoring him in a potential runoff against 37% for Flávio Bolsonaro, acting as a 'new Northeast' for the PT. Meanwhile, the 'Lava Jato generation' (ages 35–44) presents Lula’s greatest challenge, due to the operation’s association with fighting corruption during PT administrations.

item.title: VÍDEO: como são feitas as pesquisas eleitorais e como os entrevistados são escolhidos
item.description: Electoral polls are conducted using scientifically designed samples based on IBGE and TSE data, where municipalities and sectors are randomly selected and interviewees are chosen to represent the electorate by region, gender, age, education, and income. The chance of being interviewed is comparable to winning the lottery, so never having participated does not mean one's profile is unrepresented. Quaest conducts in-person, household surveys, distinguishing them from non-probabilistic polls.

item.title: Com afastamento de conselheiro, TCE no Maranhão tem três vagas travadas por decisão de Flávio Dino
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino removed Daniel Brandão from the presidency of the Maranhão Court of Accounts (TCE-MA), Brandão’s nephew and political ally of Governor Carlos Brandão. The move is part of legal actions stemming from Dino’s political rift with Brandão, now an adversary. As a result, only four of the seven seats on the TCE-MA are currently filled by titular members.

item.title: TSE se reúne para debater regras sobre deepfakes nas eleições
item.description: The TSE will meet to discuss the use of deepfakes in the 2026 elections, with a potential total ban on the technology in campaigns due to misinformation concerns. The meeting follows controversy over an AI-generated avatar of former president Jair Bolsonaro used in the PL convention that launched Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign. TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques aims to establish a common understanding on the issue, while the case involving the avatar is under the rapporteurship of Minister Estela Aranha.

item.title: Foco do bolsonarismo, pauta anti-STF é evitada por André e Derrite
item.description: Senate candidates backed by Flávio Bolsonaro, André do Prado and Guilherme Derrite, have avoided emphasizing the anti-STF agenda in their campaigns despite being aligned with Bolsonarism. Allies say they were advised not to confront the Supreme Court head-on to avoid early institutional conflict, focusing instead on public security (Derrite) and ties to the state government (André do Prado). The strategy reflects the right’s goal of securing a Senate majority to use impeachment powers against STF ministers following Jair Bolsonaro’s conviction.

item.title: Maioria do eleitorado, mulheres são apenas 35% dos candidatos em 2026
item.description: Women make up 52.84% of Brazil's electorate but only 35% of candidates in the 2026 elections, with significantly lower representation in majoritarian offices: just 33 women running for governor (16.8%), 69 for Senate (21.9%), and two for president (15%). The disparity is even more pronounced in the leading presidential tickets, none of which feature women as president or vice-president.

item.title: Engenheiro ligado a esquema de BRT ganhou cargo em estatal sob Lula
item.description: Engineer Dalton Ferracioli de Assis, under investigation since 2016 for allegedly diverting up to R$14.5 million in a BRT project in São José dos Campos that was never built, was appointed maintenance manager at Ceagesp in March 2023, three months after Lula’s inauguration. Despite an ongoing civil inquiry into illegal bidding exemptions and contracts favoring firms tied to relatives of FUSP leaders, he holds the position with a base salary of R$27,000. The São Paulo State Court of Justice (TJSP) recently accepted the MPSP’s indictment, turning him into a defendant alongside former mayor Carlinhos de Almeida (PT) and others in the scheme.

item.title: Centrão avalia peso do Congresso em distância de Flávio e pontes com Lula
item.description: Centrão parties, including União Progressista, Republicanos, and MDB, maintain formal neutrality or distance from Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) candidacy while preserving ties with President Lula’s (PT) government, aiming to maximize their congressional influence in 2027 to negotiate with whoever wins the presidency. Despite individual endorsements like Ciro Nogueira’s (PP-PI) for Flávio, the parties prioritize state and parliamentary alliances to secure post-electoral leverage regardless of the presidential outcome. This strategy echoes 2023, when Lula governed without a congressional majority and faced constant negotiation, underscoring the Centrão’s role as a kingmaker in Brazilian politics.

item.title: Veja a agenda dos candidatos à Presidência nesta terça-feira (18/8)
item.description: On Tuesday (August 18), presidential candidates held campaign events across multiple states, including meetings with supporters, interviews, engagements with organizations, and government plan presentations. Lula’s agenda was not disclosed by the report’s closing, while candidates such as Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Pablo Marçal had scheduled activities in Belo Horizonte, São Paulo, and Brasília. Agendas are subject to change and were obtained through direct contact with campaign teams.

item.title: Caminhos tortuosos
item.description: President Lula visited Amapá to inspect the site where Petrobras found indications of oil in the Amazon River Mouth, accompanied by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following a recent reconciliation mediated by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The trip was undertaken in his capacity as president, not as a re-election candidate, according to his advisors.

item.title: O vazio de um tempo nublado, sem Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign launch in Copacabana was marked by low turnout and the absence of key allies such as Silas Malafaia, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Michelle Bolsonaro. PL president Valdemar Costa Neto blamed the overcast weather for the poor attendance and publicly admitted that 'there is no one like Bolsonaro,' highlighting the campaign's reliance on Jair Bolsonaro's personal appeal. The subsequent cancellation of a motorcycle rally in Juiz de Fora, again attributed to bad weather, underscored a broader pattern of weak mobilization without the former president as the central figure.

item.title: Tarcísio manifesta solidariedade a Marina após intimidação em SP
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas expressed solidarity with candidate Marina Silva after she reported being intimidated by an aggressive man during a campaign walk in São Paulo. He stressed the importance of respecting freedom of expression and condemned any form of violence or aggression, particularly against women, stating that criminal acts must be investigated and punished.

item.title: A resposta que o TSE quer dar ao registro de candidatura de Pablo Marçal
item.description: Businessman and influencer Pablo Marçal (PRTB) announced his candidacy for President of Brazil, despite being ineligible until 2032 due to electoral court convictions. The move surprised ministers of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), which is now pushing for a rapid analysis of his registration to ensure legal certainty for voters. The TSE aims to avoid uncertainty in the 2026 election by preemptively ruling on the validity of Marçal's candidacy.

item.title: De encontros com evangélicos a início de campanha em missa, Tarcísio busca apoio de setores religiosos
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has intensified outreach to religious sectors, particularly evangelical and Catholic leaders, through meetings with figures like Apostle Estevam Hernandes and participation in religious events such as the Canção Nova Abraça São Paulo mass. His speeches emphasized faith and social responsibility, while allies like Mayor Ricardo Nunes made veiled criticisms of opponents, associating them with 'liars' and church persecutors. Tarcísio avoided direct vote appeals, focusing instead on his governance record and longstanding ties to the evangelical community.

item.title: Após Rio e SP, Eduardo Cunha tenta se eleger em MG e vira um dos mais de cem candidatos que trocaram de estado em 2026
item.description: Former Chamber of Deputies president Eduardo Cunha (Republicanos) will run for federal deputy from Minas Gerais in 2026, after no longer seeking office in Rio de Janeiro and having a failed attempt in São Paulo in 2022. He is part of a group of at least 132 candidates who changed states for this year's election, according to a GLOBO survey based on TSE data, with 117 of them also switching parties. Republicanos attracted the most of these migrants (15), followed by PL (9).

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro é a segunda ex-primeira-dama do Brasil a disputar uma eleição; saiba quem foi a primeira
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro confirms her candidacy for the Brazilian Senate from the Federal District in the 2026 elections, becoming the second former First Lady of Brazil to run for office, after Rosane Malta (formerly Collor), who ran for state deputy in Alagoas in 2018. Michelle declared assets totaling R$ 4.49 million to the Electoral Justice, including R$ 4.15 million in financial investments.

item.title: Cúpula do Congresso se reaproxima de Lula por interesses locais e evita Flávio após o caso Master
item.description: Lula has been reapproaching congressional leadership, holding recent meetings with Davi Alcolumbre and receiving explicit support from Hugo Motta. Meanwhile, PP allies such as Ciro Nogueira and Artur Lira worked to prevent the party from naming Flávio Bolsonaro’s running mate. These actions reflect a strategy to isolate Lula’s main electoral rival through local and partisan agreements.

item.title: Assassinato, suspeita de propina e disputa política: entenda a decisão de Dino que afastou sobrinho de governador do TCE-MA
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the 180-day removal of Daniel Itapary Brandão, nephew of Maranhão Governor Carlos Brandão (MDB), as president of the State Audit Court (TCE-MA), over suspicions of his involvement in a bribery scheme and obstruction of justice tied to the 2022 murder of businessman João Bosco Sobrinho. The ruling alleges Daniel used his position to solicit illicit payments and prevent the convicted assassin from disclosing Daniel’s presence at a meeting with the victim prior to the killing. His replacement, Marcelo Tavares, is a long-time ally of Dino and former Maranhão Chief of Staff.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cobra fidelidade de prefeitos a Ruas após antigos aliados declararem voto em Paes
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pressured Rio de Janeiro interior mayors to remain loyal to Douglas Ruas’s gubernatorial slate, criticizing those who switched support to Eduardo Paes (PSD) after being elected with Bolsonaro family backing in 2024. Mayor Júlio Canelinha (PSD) of Paraíba do Sul pushed back, stating his mandate owes nothing to Bolsonaro and that he switched to Paes after União Brasil abandoned a majoritarian candidacy. He also denied receiving any parliamentary amendments or institutional support from Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: De pastor suplente de Crivella a presidente de partido: quem são os candidatos mais ricos nas eleições do Rio
item.description: Pastor and lawyer Francisco Eugênio, alternate for Marcelo Crivella in the Senate race, is the wealthiest candidate in Rio de Janeiro's 2026 elections, declaring R$91 million in assets. Antonio Rueda, president of União Brasil and federal deputy candidate, follows with R$75.6 million, while Chico Machado (PL), state deputy candidate, reports R$48 million. Ideological profiles are not detailed in the provided excerpt.

item.title: Campanhas de Tarcísio e Haddad consultaram mesmo especialista em segurança
item.description: The campaigns of Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) and Fernando Haddad (PT) consulted the same public security expert, Leandro Piquet, who noted convergences in their concerns, including organized crime’s infiltration into legal sectors like fuel, money laundering, and gaming platforms, as well as the need to improve crime resolution, especially femicide investigations. Despite differing solutions, both candidates agree on the importance of inter-institutional coordination between state and municipal guards to prevent organized crime from territorial control.

item.title: Presidenciável quer proibir pesquisas que não o chamem de veterinário
item.description: Presidential candidate Wilson Grassi (Democrat) has filed legal actions against over a dozen polling institutes for failing to use his official ballot name, 'Veterinário Wilson Grassi', in electoral surveys. He argues that omitting the 'veterinarian' title undermines voter identification and biases results, requesting the TSE to ban dissemination of polls that do not correctly reference him. His campaign claims to have identified 24 ongoing polls referring to him only as 'Wilson Grassi' or 'Wilson Grassi Jr'.

item.title: 'Lei Alvinho': mudança no marco para idade mínima de deputado pode beneficiar filho de Lira e mais duas candidatas
item.description: The 'Alvinho Law', approved in October, extended the deadline for candidates to reach the minimum age of 21 to assume federal, state, or district deputy offices, allowing the requirement to be met up to 90 days after the presumed inauguration. Only three candidates benefit: Álvaro Lins Pereira de Lira (Alvinho Lira, son of former Chamber President Arthur Lira), Vitória Souza, and Manu Bim, who will turn 21 after February 1 but within the new 90-day window. The Christian Democracy party has filed a lawsuit at the STF challenging the law's constitutionality, arguing the age minimum should be verified at candidacy registration, not inauguration.

item.title: Desembargadora se declara suspeita de apreciar candidatura de Moro
item.description: Federal judge Gisele Lemke, serving as a justice in the Paraná Electoral Court (TRE-PR), declared herself disqualified from ruling on cases related to Sérgio Moro’s gubernatorial candidacy, citing her proximity to Lava Jato-era magistrates that compromises impartiality. This marks the second time she has recused herself in cases involving the former Lava Jato judge, having done so in 2023 at the TRF-4. Her prior rulings favoring Deltan Dallagnol’s candidacy were later challenged and partially suspended by Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino.

item.title: Quem são os conselheiros de Tarcísio na campanha à reeleição em SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas' re-election campaign in São Paulo is advised by specialists in public security, education, and environment, coordinated by Natália Resende. The team includes figures such as Osvaldo Nico, Henguel Ricardo Pereira, and consultants from Comunitas, which developed the 'Pacto Pelo Futuro', along with Cláudia Costin in education. Some advisors, like Leandro Piquet, have prior experience working with opposing campaigns, including Fernando Haddad's.

item.title: As cidades que podem decidir a eleição em São Paulo
item.description: An analysis of voting patterns in 645 municipalities of São Paulo from 2002 to 2022 reveals the scale of the challenge facing Fernando Haddad (PT) in his bid for governor and Lula’s re-election campaign. The study identifies key cities where the PT must concentrate efforts to counter historical Bolsonaro support in competitive regions. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Planalto cobra ministros por divulgação de ações de Lula, estabelece metas e tenta evitar restrições eleitorais
item.description: The Planalto is demanding that ministers conduct at least three weekly trips across Brazil to promote government actions under Lula, including inaugurations and regional media interviews, to maintain visibility during the electoral period while complying with electoral law. The effort aims to counter opposition narratives, such as claims that Lula inaugurated unfinished works, with particular focus on projects in Health, Education, and Transport. Ministers are also receiving guidance from Secom and SAJ to avoid public speaking missteps during these events.

item.title: Mais de 3 mil candidatos trocaram de partido desde 2022; veja as legendas que mais ganharam e perderam nomes
item.description: A g1 survey reveals that 3,681 candidates who ran in the 2022 elections are now running in 2026 under a different party, representing 58% of the total. The PL party gained the most candidates (349), while União Brasil lost the most (273). Novo recorded the highest net gain (+173), with significant inflows from PL and PTB.

item.title: 'O Brasil pronto pra mais'; 'O Brasil vai vencer' e mais: veja slogans dos candidatos à Presidência do Brasil
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential campaign officially began on Sunday (16), with candidates already revealing their slogans and campaign materials. Lula (PT) uses 'Brasil pronto pra mais', while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) opts for 'Brasil vai vencer'. Other candidates, including Renan Santos (Missão), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Romeu Zema (Novo) and Augusto Cury (Avante), have also launched their campaign slogans, now permitting explicit voter outreach through rallies, social media and paid advertisements.

item.title: Ministros do TSE se reúnem nesta terça para discutir uso de deepfakes na campanha eleitoral
item.description: The TSE met on Tuesday to discuss a potential broad or selective ban on deepfakes in electoral campaigns, favoring a total prohibition to avoid an influx of legal challenges. The meeting also considered penalties such as fines and warnings, and was prompted by a PT lawsuit against an AI-generated video showing Jair Bolsonaro at the PL convention. The debate takes place while Bolsonaro serves house arrest for his conviction in the coup plot.

item.title: Nunes Marques deve reunir ministros do TSE para debater vídeo usado por Flávio com IA de Bolsonaro e punição a deepfakes
item.description: TSE President Kássio Nunes Marques will convene ministers to discuss deepfake regulations in the 2026 electoral campaign, following an AI-generated video featuring Jair Bolsonaro's image and voice shown at Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential nomination convention by the PL party. The Court is considering a broad ban on deepfakes regardless of intent and defining penalties, with a tendency to apply fines for violations, reserving harsher sanctions for abuse or recurrence.

item.title: Flávio faz primeiro ato com Nikolas e tenta aproximá-lo de campanha, mas esbarra em agenda própria do deputado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) held his first joint event with federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) in Belo Horizonte, featuring a walk, sticker campaign, and press conference. The meeting aims to leverage Nikolas’ large digital following within bolsonarismo to support Flávio’s presidential campaign, despite Nikolas maintaining an independent agenda not always aligned with the race. Flávio’s campaign team is building a network of digitally active bolsonarist allies to amplify messages, counter attacks, and share the burden of political confrontation.

item.title: Tarcísio repudia hostilidade a Marina em ato: "Não podemos admitir"
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas condemned the hostility faced by Senate candidate Marina Silva during a campaign event with Fernando Haddad, stating that disagreements must not turn into violence or intimidation. He expressed full solidarity with Marina and emphasized the importance of respecting freedom of expression and uniting against violence against women, which he called a 'scourge'. The incident involved an unidentified man verbally attacking Marina, telling her she 'returned to the scene of the crime'.

item.title: Defesa de ex-secretário do Maranhão quer o impedimento de Dino
item.description: The defense of former Maranhão secretary Raimundo Cutrim filed a request to disqualify Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino from overseeing investigations against him, arguing Dino is himself under investigation for alleged persecution. Cutrim is probed for allegedly obstructing a 2022 homicide investigation and leaking information to journalist Luís Pablo, while Dino ordered the precautionary removal of TCE-MA President Daniel Brandão, nephew of the governor, over suspicions of interference in the probe.

item.title: Mendonça manda Lula remover das redes trechos de vídeos com pedidos explícitos de voto em convenção
item.description: TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered Lula, Jerônimo Rodrigues, and the PT to edit or remove YouTube video excerpts containing explicit vote requests made during the Bahia state convention, ruling they constitute premature electoral propaganda. The decision partially grants a Novo party petition but rejects total removal of the content. Lula urged votes for himself, Jerônimo, Wagner, and Rui Costa, emphasizing that electoral law permits no exception for intraparty settings when speech includes direct or semantically equivalent calls to vote.

item.title: TSE registra maior queda de candidaturas em 3 décadas, sob efeito de federações e de partido de Marçal
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) recorded the largest drop in candidacies for the 2026 general elections since 1994, driven by the formation of party federations and the influence of Pablo Marçal’s new party. This trend reflects a strategic reorganization of Brazil’s political landscape, with fewer isolated candidacies and greater concentration in alliances.
